youtubeTitle: The Gospel and Soul Health Session 4 - Dr Bruce Wauchope
chapter: 3rd Non-negotiable: The Eternal Son is the One in whom this love story will be completed; 4th Non-negotiable: We are made in, by and through the Eternal Son, sustained and held together by Him; He shares His life with us
topic: Made and sustained in Christ's life
summary: Bruce argues that if we start from the wrong place, with our own constructs instead of the Trinity's identity and purpose, we end up with logical but meaningless 'gobbledygook', like typing with fingers one key off. The Word, the eternal Son, is the one in whom the love story will be completed. All things were made in, through and for him, and are sustained by his zoe; there is no 'outside' of God as Greek philosophy assumes. Following Cyril of Alexandria's reading of John 1:3-4, creation has the gift of Christ's life in it. Darkness is not the absence of light but blindness to love while Christ's life still flows; life lived in love makes more life, while life put through the 'blender' of our darkness makes death. Religion, a self-made light, is a great darkness, and Jesus came to penetrate our darkness in his own body and heal the split in humanity from within.
keyPoints: Start from the wrong place and you get the wrong answer. Like typing with fingers shifted one key over, you produce orderly but meaningless 'gobbledygook' while feeling completely right.
Pre-creation scriptures are the blueprint for interpreting creation. Bruce's levelled playground made sense only once you knew the plan.
Greek philosophy puts God and matter in eternal separation. In truth, matter came out of nothing in the middle of God, and there is no outside to God.
The third non-negotiable: the Word (Yeshua, Jesus) is the one who becomes human and completes the love story, never without the Father and the Spirit.
The fourth non-negotiable: everything is made in, through, by and for the Word and is sustained by him. We do not have life in ourselves; the Trinity does.
Colossians 1:16 should read 'in him all things were created', not merely 'by him'. Cyril of Alexandria reads John 1:3-4 as 'that which came into being, in it was life'.
Creation has Christ's uncreated life in it. Bruce says this is needed for understanding biology and the 'field structures' of nature; it is perichoresis, not pantheism.
Darkness is not the absence of light. Christ's life flows in it, and it has intelligence, will and drive, but it is blind to love. Sexual desire acted on without love, for example, hurts people.
Life lived in love makes more life. Life lived in partial light makes partial life, and Christ's life put through the blender of our darkness makes death.
Darkness works like a judo throw, using the power of Christ's own life. The Trinity tolerates this and works from the bottom up because they want to be loved back, not obeyed through force.

Religion is a self-referential layer of darkness: broken cisterns (Jeremiah 2:13) and self-kindled sparks (Isaiah 50:11). The torment is the natural result of our own way, not the Father taking a stick to us.
Jesus penetrated our blindness in his own body to meet the Father and the Spirit within himself, healing the split in humanity ('the ruler of this world has nothing in me').

keyTerms.definition: Christ's uncreated life, given to and flowing through all creation.
Union with distinction: creation shares Christ's life without becoming God.
Blindness to love while Christ's life still flows; it has will, drive and intelligence.
A self-referential, self-made light for climbing back to God; a 'great darkness'.
The 'factory' that twists Christ's life in darkness, which Jesus came to heal.
Bruce's image for darkness using the power of Christ's own life to do harm.
Creation does not possess life in itself but is continually held and given life by the Son.

quotes: If you start from the wrong place you'll end up with the wrong answer.
There is no separation. There is only blindness to the love, life and light of Father, Son and Spirit.
Life lived in love makes more life.
The false light of religion is the great darkness.

caseStudy.title: Gifted but destructive
caseStudy.scenario: Sam, 50, is a brilliant, driven entrepreneur. His energy and talent built a successful company, but his staff are burnt out, his marriage is strained, and he uses people to reach his goals. He attends church and is proud of his strict moral standards, yet feels empty and irritable. A health scare has forced him to slow down.
caseStudy.analysis: In Bruce's terms, Sam's drive and gifts are Christ's zoe flowing through him, but lived without love they become a 'judo throw' that creates harm and death in relationships. His moralistic religion is a self-made light that keeps him blind. What's missing isn't capability but love; when that is received, the same capacities can flow towards life.
pathway: Recognise that his energy and talent are received gifts rather than self-generated.
Ask his wife and staff honestly where his drive has hurt them, and listen without defending himself.
Replace moral self-assessment with the question: 'Is this lived in love?'
Build regular rest and reflection into his week as an act of receiving rather than producing.
Follow his doctor's advice and consider coaching or counselling around his work patterns.

practices.name: Life-or-death audit
practices.how: At day's end, note one place your energy was lived in love (more life) and one where it wasn't (death). Hand both to Christ.

practices.name: Received-life gratitude
practices.how: List five abilities or desires you have, and thank Christ for each as his life flowing through you.

practices.name: Spot the self-made sparks
practices.how: Ask where you rely on religious performance for security, and pray Isaiah 50:10-11 honestly.

reflection: Where might you be starting from the wrong place and producing confident 'gobbledygook'?
Which of your strengths are currently being lived without love?
How does seeing religion as a possible darkness challenge your own practice?
